title: C482/120/2008 of PRATAP SINGH and OTHERS Vs STATE and ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
CRIMINAL MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATION No. 120/2008
(Under Section 482 of the CrPC)
Pratap Singh & Others ÖÖ.Applicants
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & Another ÖÖRespondents
27th February, 2013
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention that
there is no representation on behalf of the
complainant/respondent no. 2 despite personal service.
Hence, this Court rendered hearing to Mr. Pankaj Negi,
Advocate, holding brief of Mr. NS Negi, Advocate for the
accused applicants and Mr. PS Saun, AGA, for the State.
Also perused the papers on record.
2. The challenge in present criminal miscellaneous
application is to the order of cognizance dated 31.10.2007,
passed by the Judicial Magistrate, Purola, District
Uttarkashi, whereby accused applicants have been
summoned to stand trial for the offences under Section 147,
420, 504, 506 IPC.
3. Brief facts of the case are that a complaint was
filed by Chattar Singh, respondent no. 2, against present
accused applicants and three other accused persons.
Complainant examined himself under Section 200 CrPC on
22.8.2007 and his witnesses, namely, Birbal Singh and
Bhajan Singh were examined under Section 202 CrPC on
21.9.2007. After perusing the statements of complainant
and his aforenamed witnesses, learned Magistrate passed
the impugned order of cognizance.

2
4. Having heard learned Counsel for the applicants
and learned State Counsel and on going through the
averments made in the complaint, it appears that the
alleged incident took place on 12.8.2007, on which date
accused persons hurled abuses on the complainant and
held out a treat to kill him. However, specific place and time
of incident have not been mentioned by the complainant.
The complaint too was filed after nine days of alleged
incident, wherefor no explanation has been offered in the
complaint.
5. Accused applicants belong to State of Himachal
Pradesh, residing close to interstate border with State of
Uttarakhand. Complainant is from State of Uttarakhand
having his residence and land in District Uttarkashi at
adjoining interstate border with the State of Himachal
Pradesh. After revenue purchase of a piece of land in
district Uttarkashi, situated adjacent to land of
complainant, an apple orchard was developed by the
applicants. It has been alleged that applicants encroached
upon the land of complainant and on their instructions and
instigation, other accused persons uprooted as many as
150 apple trees of the complainant. Subsequently, an
agreement took place to compensate the losses suffered by
the complainant, but the same was not complied with.
6. I have gave my thoughtful consideration to
arguments of learned Counsel and other papers on record.
The allegations made in the complaint are vague in nature
and full of embellishments and embroidery. It appears that
the complainant dragged the accused persons in the
present litigation just to harass them and to settle his

3
personal score. The impugned complaint is nothing but
utter abuse of the process of Court, and it cannot be
permitted to proceed any further.
7. Consequently, this criminal miscellaneous
application, filed under Section 482 CrPC, is allowed.
Impugned order of cognizance dated 31.10.2007, passed by
the Judicial Magistrate, Purola, District Uttarkashi as well
as the entire proceedings of Criminal Complaint Case No.
260/2007, Chattar Singh v. Pratap Singh & Others, under
Section 147, 420, 504, 506 IPC, are hereby quashed.
8. Inform the court below accordingly.
